en: Pīṭhastava 1: Brahmāṇī, whose nature is the ultimate reality, resounds with various deep tones; Ghoracaṇḍī and Raudrī;
Kaumārī, desiring fame; and Vaiṣṇavī, singing, indeed drinks the intoxication of honey.
May Vārāhī, playing upon the most resonant drums; Aindrī dancing;
Cāmuṇḍā; and Lakṣmī, together with the hosts of Śiva—may these Mothers purify you.
[1] And may Gaṇapati, Heramba, Vighnarāja, and Vināyaka [purify you]. [2]
The son of a god, possessed of great heroism and great strength and prowess.
The leader of the Gaṇas, who has a large belly and a massive body, who possesses a single tusk and an elephantine face, who is white in color, of great brilliance, and has three eyes. || 3 ||
A rosary and the gesture of granting boons are held in his right hands;
an axe and a skull-bowl are held in his left hands.
The god who delights in various flowers, who is anointed with various fragrances, whose body has a serpent as a sacred thread, and who is the destroyer of various obstacles. || 5 ||

I bow to the destroyer of obstacles, who is worshipped by gods, asuras, and humans, as well as by siddhas, gandharvas, and kinnaras, and who wears a mouse as his emblem (Mūṣakāṭa). Brahmāṇī, Brahmasāvitrī, she who knows the true nature of Brahman.
She has four arms, four faces, and is devoted to the four deities.
On the fourteenth day, she is long-lasting and pervasive, benefiting the world throughout the four ages;
seated upon a celestial chariot drawn by swans, the Grandmother (Pitāmahī) possesses a gentle form.
Holding a book and a garland of flowers, and bestowing the boons of granting wishes and fearlessness;
the goddess is devoted to yellow flowers, with yellow limbs and a yellow-like complexion.
She is accompanied by yellow offerings, anointed with yellow perfumes,
residing in the Udumbara tree, and dwelling in the sacred field of Prayāga.
Salutations to you, the eternal Brahman-śakti residing in the eastern seat;
salutations to the great goddess Māheśvarī, who destroys delusion, illusion, and passion.
Mounted upon a great bull, resounding with the great syllable *huṃ*,
her body resembles refined gold, and she is crowned with a skull and the moon.
She has three eyes and holds a trident, a rosary, and a water-pot;
her entire body is adorned with various ornaments, and she grants boons with her right hand.
The Goddess of the lords of all, who is in every way the cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction;
she is devoted to white flowers and is anointed with white perfumes.
Clad in white garments and adorned with mudrās and ornaments,
she dwells beneath a *tāla* tree in the great sacred field of Vārāṇasī. (15)
O Māheśvarī, established upon the northern seat, salutations be to you!
In your childhood state, you are Mahāraudrī; as Kaumārī, you have blood-red eyes. 16.
The auspicious goddess wears a red hue, her form crimson as vermilion;
she has four arms and holds a spear, a thread, and a vessel of the perfected ones.
Kaumārī is the supreme Śakti, who rides upon an excellent peacock;
she is clothed in red garments and subsists on blood, flesh, and marrow. || 18 ||
O Kaumārī, who dwells in the banyan tree within the great sacred field of Kolāpura, who eternally resides upon the seat of fire— to you, salutations again and again!
O Vaiṣṇavī, you who are the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu and the destroyer of the wicked Daityas!
Her limbs are greenish-dark in color, and she is seated upon Garuḍa. || 20 ||
Holding a conch, a discus, and a mace in her hands, adorned with four arms, possessing great play amidst red flames, she is decorated with various ornaments. || 21 ||
She possesses the fragrance of green flowers and wears green garments;
she dwells in the Kadamba tree within the great field of Aṭṭahāsa.
She is established in the form of a presence in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld.
Standing on a seat in the southwest, O Nārāyaṇī, salutations be to you!
(23) Vārāhī has a terrible red body, red hair, and a large belly;
she is formidable with her tusks, deep-voiced, red-eyed, and three-eyed. (24)
She wears a garland of skulls adorned with various flowers;
she is mounted upon a great boar and possesses a radiance equal to blazing fire. || 25 ||
Adorned with a goad, a razor, a staff, and a ḍāmaru as ornaments, she has three eyes, a blazing body, and destroys the pride of the wicked. (26)
O you who reside in the field of Jayantī, who take shelter in the nimba tree,
who are eternally situated on the southern seat in the form of a boar— salutations be to you!
O Śakreśvarī, you who possess a thousand eyes and a body as ruddy as saffron.
The sovereign lady of the gods, the goddess of the gods, adorned with every ornament.
Four-armed and large-eyed, holding a parasol and a bell, the goddess Mahāvajradharā stands upon the elephant Airāvata. (29)
The goddess delights in various flowers, is adorned with various jewels, her limbs are anointed with various perfumes, and she shines in various garments. || 30 ||
O Śakreśvarī, who resides eternally upon a Nāga-pīṭha in the great field of Cīrakṣetra, situated among Karañja trees—homage be to you! 31.
You are Cāmuṇḍā, Caṇḍikā, Caṇḍī, and the exceedingly fierce Surasundarī.
Caṇḍāṭṭahāsā, Caṇḍākṣī, Pracaṇḍā, and Caṇḍanāśinī. || 32 ||
Her fangs were formidable, her body was red, her hair was tawny, and she had a large belly;
she was emaciated, terrifying, fierce, and frightening with her lolling tongue.
Seated upon a great corpse-throne, she is beautifully adorned with eight arms;
in her hands she holds a sword and shield, and she carries a hand-drum and a khaṭvāṅga staff.

Holding a khaṭvāṅga and a skull-cup in her hands, adorned with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, her entire body decorated with ornaments of human bone, she is the beloved who bestows the destruction of enemies. 35.
Resembling a thousand suns at every planting pit,
she was filled with garlands of flames, her body possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns.

O you who dwell in the great field of Akṣa, the single Aśvattha tree, surrounded by spirits, vetālas, ḍākinīs, and rākṣasas, and who reside at the sacred seat (pīṭha) in the region of Maruta— homage be to you, O Cāmuṇḍā! (37) 10
The great goddess Mahālakṣmī, rich in enjoyments and beautiful in her virtues,
is wise and seated upon a throne, mounted on sandals made of cat's-eye gem.
The goddess has four arms and large eyes; she holds a sword and a shield, carries a vessel and a drop [of nectar], and is adorned with necklaces and a pair of earrings. (39)
Her entire body was inlaid with jewels, she was adorned with a crest-jewel,
possessed various flowers and gems, and was clothed in garments and anointed with perfumes.
The Goddess pervades the three worlds; she dwells in all things, both moving and unmoving;
she is bowed to by the Siddhas and Gandharvas, and worshipped by the Vidyādharas and gods. 41.
O Varā Balā, who resides at Plakṣasaṃsthā in the great sacred field of Devīkoṭa;
O Mahālakṣmī, who dwells in the seat of Īśāna—salutations be to you!
You are the mother of all Buddhas and the bringer of satisfaction to all.
You alone possess all forms, and you alone are the one whose form is the universe.
Bhairava is terrifying, formidable, and fierce, possessing a form that is both awe-inspiring and profound;
his body resembles the stainless [sky], a great festival of all desires. (44)
Adorned with many arms, wearing various garments, and auspicious,
she was tawny-haired with half her locks flowing loose, possessing a splendor equal to a forest fire.
Trilocanā, possessed of great splendor and radiance equal to fire and the sun,

holds a trident, a severed head, a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), a hand-drum (ḍamaru), a raised index finger, and a banner; she is auspicious, bearing wisdom and its book, as well as a sword and a shield.
The god who holds a noose and a goad, and who bears the great vajra-needle.
Holding a skull-bowl, a flaying knife, and a wheel, he is draped in an elephant hide,
his face made terrifying by fangs, and his waist encircled by a tiger skin.
Adorned with ornaments on all her limbs and beautified by flowers made of human bones, the Goddess wears a garland of heads; she is the auspicious one within the hollow of the Kāpālika.
Wearing a crest-jewel of great splendor and a skull adorned with the moon,
she is always led as the beloved one, eternally seated upon a great corpse.
Resembling a thousand suns, she is endowed with the mark of a parasol.
She dwells eternally in the four seats and resides in the eight fields. || 51 ||
The Goddess, who abides in the eight forms, is beloved by the eight Yoginīs;
she dwells eternally upon the auspicious throne (Bhadrapīṭha), surrounded by Bhadrakālī.
O Vīrabhadra, you are the agent who brings about auspiciousness; salutations be unto you!
Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, and Krodhabhairava; || 53 ||
To Unmattabhairava, Kapālī, Bhīṣaṇa,
and Saṃhārabhairava— to you, the eight Bhairavas, let there be obeisance.
(54) O you who abide in your own place, who possess your own authority, who are your own essential nature, and who are your own heroes!
Those dwelling on earth do not possess their own clear tree-like canopy, nor indeed divine eyes.
O protector of the fields of the ten directions, O [protector of] the fourteen fields,
O protector of the fifty fields— homage be to you, Kṣetrapāla! O Lord of lords, Great Lord, Primordial Lord, O one of great intelligence!
O Śrīnātha, Siddhanātha, Mīnanātha, homage be to you! || 57 ||
O Lord of the Field, Lord of the Sacred Seats, Great-Souled Lord of the Island, Lord of the Pretas, Lord of the Spirits, Lord of the Waves, homage be to you! || 58 ||
Salutations to you, the Lord of Three, the Lord of Nine, and the supreme Lord of Sixteen;
salutations to you, the twenty-seven, the fifty-five, and the eighty-four.
You are the imperishable eye, the abode of the ship, and likewise the Hero of all the Siddhanāthas; therefore, let there be salutation to you. (60) 17.
The man who recites this once, twice, or thrice—
By reciting this one hundred times, one attains the supreme fruit.
It shall destroy grief, anxiety, and the like; it shall destroy the entire circle of obstacles;
it shall destroy diseases and quarrels; it shall destroy suffering and what is difficult to accomplish.
It shall destroy fear and poverty; it shall destroy the fear born of enemies;
it shall destroy [the threat of] fire, thieves, and the like; and it shall destroy that which arises from the king's wrath.
It shall destroy terrible conflict and malevolent sorcery performed by others;
it shall destroy hatred, passion, and the like, and it shall destroy all sins. || 64 ||
It increases longevity, health, sovereignty, wealth, and grain;
it augments dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, as well as fame and good fortune. (65)
May he increase day by day his supernatural power, accomplishment, glory, fortune, learning, knowledge, sons and the like, intellect, progeny, and excellent friends. (66)
It always destroys untimely death and calamities;
all diseases are pacified, and long life is attained. (67)
The hymn of praise to the Śrīpīṭha is completed.
